newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila shares end lower for fourth straight day.
newsitem.headline: Manila shares end lower for fourth straight day.

text.p: Philippine shares fell to a new 17-month low on Tuesday after an early rally gave way to profit-taking, brokers said.
"It's the same old story. Everybody wants out of the market until the FOMC meeting," said Cilette Liboro, research head at Orion-Squire Capital Inc.
The main index closed 9.98 points lower, or 0.40 percent at 2,499.38. In early trade, it briefly rose over one percent.

"No one is taking a long-term stance. There's the constant comparison with Thailand and only time can answer the fundamental questions on the economy," said Regina Manzano, analyst at Philippine Asia Equity.
In the broader market, there were 86 decliners against 36 gainers and 58 issues were unchanged.

The property sub-index was the most battered for the day, falling over two percent still on fears of rising interest rates and its negative effect on the interest rate-sensitive real estate market, analysts said.

"We expected the brief rally since investors are still wary about local and global scenario. Tomorrow's trade will depend much on the FOMC meeting tonight," said Helen Alvarez, research head at All Asia Securities.
Traders said the market will likely test the 2,450 support level on Wednesday.
